name: Mesalazine
route_note: Delayed- or extended-release oral tablets, capsules or granules; enemas, foams and suppositories for distal colitis
originator: Identified as the active moiety of sulfasalazine by Azad Khan, Piris and Truelove (Oxford)

discovery.by: A. K. Azad Khan, J. Piris and S. C. Truelove
discovery.note: Showed that 5-ASA, not sulfapyridine, is the therapeutically active part of sulfasalazine in ulcerative colitis.

tagline: Gut-targeted 5-ASA, first-line therapy for mild to moderate ulcerative colitis
summary: Mesalazine (mesalamine) is 5-aminosalicylic acid, the active component of sulfasalazine, formulated for release in the small bowel or colon. It is first-line therapy to induce and maintain remission in mild to moderate ulcerative colitis.
mechanism: Mesalazine acts topically on the inflamed colonic mucosa. Proposed mechanisms include activation of PPAR-γ, inhibition of NF-κB, reduced production of prostaglandins and leukotrienes via cyclo-oxygenase and lipoxygenase, and scavenging of reactive oxygen species.
Its effect depends on mucosal concentration, so formulations use pH-dependent coatings, time-release granules or rectal delivery to reach the affected bowel.
uses: Induction and maintenance of remission in mild to moderate ulcerative colitis
Mild Crohn's disease (some formulations and regions)

history.title: Active moiety identified
history.detail: An Oxford study shows 5-ASA is the active component of sulfasalazine.

history.title: Once-daily MMX
history.detail: FDA approves Lialda, a once-daily multi-matrix formulation.

pk.metabolism: N-acetylation (NAT1) in intestinal mucosa and liver

facts: Renal function is monitored during long-term mesalazine treatment.
Without a protective formulation, oral 5-ASA would be absorbed in the upper small bowel before reaching the colon.
